data.title: FMCG players expect emerging distribution channels to post strong growth for Q2 FY27
data.description:
Leading FMCG players witnessed strong growth momentum in alternative distribution channels which includes quick commerce, e-commerce and modern trade. In recent quarters, FMCG players have been reporting strong acceleration in sales in the overall e-commerce channel led by quick-commerce platforms.

As per quarterly update for Q2FY27, AWL Agribusiness indicated that alternate channel, consisting of modern trade, quick-commerce and e-commerce, delivered “double-digit growth”. “Within food & FMCG, key categories continued to gain traction across e-commerce and quick commerce, collectively delivering 40 per cent year-on-year growth. AWL has established a meaningful presence across these channels, with average market shares of over 10 per cent in Atta, over 25 per cent in Besan, over 40 per cent in Soya Nuggets, and around 15–20 per cent across Sugar, Suji and Poha,” the company added. It also said that execution metrics such as product fill rate and customer retention saw improvement during the quarter, supported by better assortment and availability.

In a BSE filing, Dabur India noted that “emerging channels comprising e-commerce and quick commerce are expected to report “strong growth momentum” in Q2FY27, led by its continued investments and focus on an omni-channel distribution approach. “Modern trade continues to grow at double digits. General trade continued to grow across both urban and rural markets, with rural continuing to outpace urban, led by continued efforts under Project Saksham,” the company added.

Honasa Consumer Ltd, known for brands such as Mamaearth, also noted in its Q2 update that the online channel witnessed “continued growth” momentum during the quarter. It added that general trade and modern trade channels are also expected to post strong growth on the back of its focus on garnering deeper offline distribution.

According to estimates by NielsenIQ, the overall e-commerce channel’s share grew to 7 per cent of pan-India FMCG sales in the June quarter. E-commerce channel share of FMCG sales in the top eight metros was pegged at 21 per cent. At the same time in the top 52 metros, the online channel’s share of industry sales was estimated at 21 per cent in the June quarter.

data.title: PM Narendra Modi in Chennai on Sunday for a series of engagements
data.description:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be in Chennai on Sunday October 11 for a series of events including the flag off of a new section of the Chennai Metro and inauguration of projects.

As per an official government statement, at around 11.30 am, he will undertake a ride on the Chennai Metro from Porur Bypass Station to Poonamallee Bypass Station and back. He will likely be joined by TN CM Joseph Vijay for this ride. He will also inaugurate the new Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around ₹4,900 crore.

Then, he will perform Darshan and Pooja at the Jalakandeswarar Temple in Chennai. Thereafter, he will take a walkthrough of the Brain Centre at IIT Madras.

This will be followed by the Prime Minister laying the foundation stone , inaugurating and dedicating various development projects worth over ₹13,000 crore. He will also address the gathering at this occasion.

Finally, the PM will also participate in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Chennai.

inaugurate projects

He will lay the foundation stone of and inaugurate key National Highway projects worth around ₹3,700 crore.

Prime Minister will dedicate and inaugurate railway infrastructure projects worth over ₹750 crore.

He will also inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of several port-related projects in Tamil Nadu to strengthen maritime infrastructure, expand cargo-handling capacity and improve logistics efficiency. This includes four infrastructure projects at Chennai Port: a Paved Storage Yard, four EXIM Godowns, an upgraded Cruise Terminal and a Seafarers Club.

Further, PM Modi will lay the foundation stone of the Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) project at the existing Manali Refinery of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd (CPCL) in Chennai. With a total cost of around ₹1,620 crore and a capacity of 270 thousand tonnes per annum , the project aims to produce Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks for the manufacture of world-class, premium-quality lubricants in India.

At the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre (SGBC) at IIT Madras, he is also set to launch its pioneering global scientific mission to map more than 100 human brains into three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution, across the human lifespan — from the foetal stage to old age.

data.title: Ether ETFs extend outflow streak to nine days as Solana funds snap record 14-week inflow run
data.description:
U.S. spot ether (ETH) ETFs recorded $542.1 million in net outflows last week, their worst week since January, while spot Solana (SOL) ETFs ended a record 14-week inflow streak, according to The Block's analysis of SoSoValue data.

The ether funds have now posted outflows for nine consecutive trading days, a run worth $697.2 million that began on Sept. 29.

Spot Solana ETFs lost $24.8 million over the week, the largest weekly outflow since the products launched in late October 2025.

Combined with bitcoin ETF redemptions, the three categories lost about $1.25 billion last week.

Ether funds post second straight losing week

BlackRock's ETHA, the largest ether fund by assets under management, lost $477.0 million over the week, about 88% of the category's total, per SoSoValue data. It was the fund's largest weekly outflow since mid-December 2025 and its third-largest since launching in July 2024. Grayscale's ETHE had the second-largest weekly outflow among ether funds, at $31.9 million.

Tuesday was the heaviest single trading day for the ether products, with $201.9 million in redemptions, all from ETHA. That was the fund's largest single-day outflow since Jan. 21 of this year. Tuesday's outflow came on the day ETHA's 1-for-3 reverse share split took effect.

ETHA posted outflows in all five sessions. The fund holds $8.64 billion in net assets, about $4.15 billion less than its $12.79 billion in cumulative net inflows.

The category's weekly total outflows were the largest since the week ending Jan. 23, when the funds lost $611.2 million. It was also the second straight negative week for ether ETFs, after $138.0 million left the funds the week before. Fidelity's FETH accounted for $74.1 million of that prior-week total, per the data.

Daily ether ETF flows have been negative in every session since Sept. 28, when the funds took in $17.1 million. The ether outflows began on Sept. 29, one day before bitcoin ETFs ended a nine-day, $3.1 billion inflow streak. ETHA accounted for $506.1 million of the nine-day streak's outflows.

The run ties a June 17-30 streak as the third-longest in the funds' history. The record is a 17-day stretch from May 11 to June 3 of this year, which pulled about $900.1 million from the products.

Spot ether ETF net assets fell 10% over the week to $15.71 billion. Cumulative net inflows since launch stand at $13.26 billion. The funds are still positive for 2026, with $931.8 million in net inflows year to date, down from $1.47 billion a week earlier.

Trading volume rose to $5.18 billion from $3.57 billion the previous week.

Solana funds end record inflow run

The Solana products recorded outflows in all five sessions last week, their longest daily outflow streak on record, per SoSoValue's data. Their previous longest outflow streak was three days.

Bitwise's BSOL, the largest Solana fund with $1.20 billion in net assets, lost $20.9 million over the week, about 84% of the category's outflows, per the data. It was BSOL's largest weekly outflow on record, topping a $17.0 million outflow in the week ending July 31.

Monday's $9.2 million outflow was the largest of the week. Morgan Stanley's MSOL and Invesco's QSOL were the only Solana funds to post weekly inflows, taking in a combined $2.0 million.

The $24.8 million weekly outflow is roughly three times the previous record of $8.9 million, set in the week ending Feb. 6. The funds had not posted a negative week since the week ending June 26, when they lost $1.8 million. The 14-week inflow streak topped a 13-week run that started at launch and ended in late January.

The reversal comes two weeks after the Solana funds drew a record $188.2 million in weekly inflows.

Spot Solana ETF net assets fell to $1.73 billion from $1.90 billion a week earlier. The funds held a record $1.96 billion on Sept. 25. Cumulative net inflows stand at $1.58 billion, including $816.8 million so far in 2026.

Bitcoin funds snap three-week inflow streak

Spot bitcoin (BTC) ETFs lost $681.1 million last week, ending three straight weeks of inflows, per SoSoValue data. It was their worst week since the week ending June 26, when they shed $1.79 billion.

Wednesday accounted for most of the outflows, with $487.1 million leaving the funds. The products returned to inflows on Friday with $21.1 million.

The bitcoin funds' 2026 net inflows fell to $494.1 million from $1.18 billion a week earlier. The category turned positive for the year in late September.

Bitcoin ETFs hold $105.84 billion in net assets and have drawn $57.11 billion in cumulative net inflows since launch.

Ether traded near $2,506 on Saturday morning, while SOL changed hands around $110.50 and bitcoin sat near $82,900.

The Nifty rose 1.30%, while the Sensex advanced 1.23%. Bank Nifty also recovered, gaining 1.36%. The rally was led by IT stocks following Tata Consultancy Services' September-quarter results, with buying extending to FMCG, auto and financial shares.

The macroeconomic backdrop remains challenging. Brent crude continued to trade above $100 a barrel, while WTI remained above $90. Comments from the US president on discussions with Iran offered some temporary relief, but tensions around the Strait of Hormuz and concerns over regional energy infrastructure have kept the risk of supply disruptions elevated. For India, persistently high oil prices pose risks to inflation, the import bill and the rupee.

Foreign investor selling remains a significant overhang. FIIs recorded net outflows of approximately Rs.39,779 crore in October so far, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) bought around Rs.40,355 crore over the same period, broadly offsetting the foreign selling. Domestic institutional demand has provided an important cushion, absorbing much of the pressure from overseas investors and helping stabilise the market.

Sumeet Bagadia, Executive Director at Choice Broking, believes the Nifty 50 chart pattern is signalling improving short-term sentiment, although the broader structure remains weak below key moving averages. He said that PCR at 0.98 suggests a balanced derivatives setup, while India VIX eased to 14.375, reflecting reduced volatility. Bagadia said that a strong bullish candle highlights renewed demand at lower levels, though the index remains below its key moving averages.

On the daily timeframe, the stock has undergone steady price contraction within this wedge formation, finding solid support at the lower boundary and defending its multi-month base. data.title: Indian stock markets snap 8-week losing streak - What's next for Sensex, Nifty? Triggers, strategy ​for investors
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Indian equity markets ended their eight-week losing streak, the longest in 25 years, after a volatile week in which benchmarks recovered on buying in information technology (IT), fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), automobile and financial stocks. However, persistent foreign fund outflows, elevated crude oil prices, rising global bond yields and uncertainty over the monetary policy outlook continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

For the week, the BSE Sensex gained 562.63 points, or 0.78%, to close at 72,472.33, while the Nifty 50 advanced 98.5 points, or 0.43%, to settle at 22,520.45.

The recovery gathered momentum on Friday, October 9, when the Sensex surged 879.09 points, or 1.23%, to 72,472.33. The Nifty 50 climbed 288.65 points, or 1.30%, to end at 22,520.45, snapping the benchmarks' eight-week losing streak.

"Markets snapped an eight-week losing streak, posting modest weekly gains as easing crude oil prices and positive corporate updates supported a late-week recovery. However, volatility remained elevated following the RBI's decision to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and shift its policy stance towards calibrated tightening," said Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research, Religare Broking.

Despite the rebound, market participants will look for stronger follow-through buying to determine whether the recovery can extend into the coming week. Several domestic and global developments, including inflation data, corporate earnings, crude oil prices and foreign investor flows, are likely to influence the market's direction.

Inflation data from the US will be a key trigger for global equity markets next week. US consumer inflation, core inflation, producer price inflation (PPI) and retail-sales figures will offer fresh cues on the health of the economy and the likely trajectory of the Federal Reserve's monetary policy.

Stronger-than-expected inflation readings could keep US Treasury yields and the dollar elevated, potentially putting pressure on emerging-market equities.

Crude oil remains one of the most important macroeconomic variables for Indian equities because of its implications for the country's import bill, inflation, corporate margins and currency.

Brent crude was trading above $100 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) was above $90, according to the market assessment provided. Uncertainty surrounding Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and regional energy infrastructure has also raised concerns about possible supply disruptions.

A sustained increase in crude oil prices could put pressure on India's external balance and the rupee, while raising input and transportation costs for companies. This could complicate the inflation outlook and affect expectations around interest rates.

Investors will also track September consumer price inflation (CPI) and wholesale price inflation (WPI) data in India for indications of domestic price pressures and their implications for monetary policy.

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) remained net sellers for the seventh consecutive week, offloading equities worth Rs.30,294.29 crore. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs), meanwhile, purchased equities worth Rs.30,313.48 crore during the week, providing a cushion against overseas selling.

Persistent FII outflows remain an overhang for the market, particularly if global bond yields stay elevated or the dollar strengthens. At the same time, continued domestic institutional buying could help absorb some of the selling pressure and limit further declines.

Currency movements will remain important as well. The Indian rupee depreciated by 41 paise during the week ended October 9 to close at 96.73 against the US dollar, compared with 96.32 on October 1. It traded in a range of 96.22-96.85 during the week, moving closer to its all-time low of 96.96.

Continued rupee weakness could add to imported inflation and influence foreign investor sentiment.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) recently raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and shifted its policy stance towards calibrated tightening. While the rate increase was broadly in line with expectations, the change in stance has raised concerns about borrowing costs and the possibility of further policy action.

The RBI's upward revision of its FY27 GDP growth forecast, however, provided some reassurance about the resilience of the domestic economy.

IT stocks led Friday's market recovery after Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) reported its September-quarter results, helping lift the broader indices.

Attention will now shift to HCL Technologies, Wipro and Tech Mahindra, whose quarterly results and management commentary could influence sentiment towards the sector.

Investors will look for updates on demand conditions, client spending, deal momentum, margins and business outlook. Strong corporate commentary could help sustain the rebound in IT stocks, while cautious guidance could limit gains.

The broader September-quarter earnings season will also gather momentum, with Hero MotoCorp and Nestle India among the companies scheduled to announce results. Their performance and commentary on demand, input costs and margins will provide further insight into corporate earnings trends.

The end of the eight-week losing streak marks a break in the recent downward trend, but it does not by itself confirm a sustained market reversal. Elevated crude oil prices, foreign investor selling and global macroeconomic uncertainty continue to pose risks.

Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research at Religare Broking, identified the 22,200-22,400 zone as a crucial support area to monitor. According to Mishra, holding above this region could support a recovery towards 23,000-23,300. Conversely, a decisive break below the support zone could trigger renewed weakness towards 21,700-22,000.

These levels will be important for traders assessing whether the recent rebound has enough strength to continue. Market breadth and buying participation across sectors will also help determine whether the gains extend beyond selective buying and short-covering.

"Traders should remain selective, avoid excessive leverage and adhere to disciplined risk management. Investors should prioritise companies with resilient earnings, strong balance sheets and pricing power, while considering staggered accumulation at appropriate valuations," suggested the expert.

The coming week will be important in determining whether the recovery can gain traction after the Nifty and Sensex ended their eight-week losing streak. India's September CPI and WPI inflation data, US inflation and retail-sales figures, corporate earnings, crude oil prices and geopolitical developments will be among the key triggers, noted Mishra.

Investors will also track FII and DII activity, rupee movements and US Treasury yields for signs of whether the broader risk environment is improving.

data.title: Hospital group files lawsuit to stop 340B rebate pilot again
data.description:
The American Hospital Association has once again filed a lawsuit to halt a new pilot that tests a revised rebate model for the 340B Drug Pricing Program, a federal benefits program for underinsured and low-income Americans.

The AHA, the Maine Hospital Association, and four safety-net hospitals filed the suit on Thursday, naming the Health and Human Services Department and the Health Resources and Services Administration, the HHS unit overseeing the program, among its defendants.

The lawsuit was filed in a federal court in Maine days after the HRSA announced the pilot, which allows 10 pharmaceutical manufacturers to offer after-the-fact rebates instead of upfront discounts on 21 drugs purchased under the program.

The Trump administration’s first 340B rebate pilot, which applied to only 10 medicines, was blocked by a federal judge in December following a lawsuit from the AHA and several hospital systems. The HHS formally withdrew the plan in January after losing on appeal.

The latest complaint seeks a temporary and permanent block on the program, which is set to take effect on Jan. 1 with the participation of drugmakers including AbbVie , Amgen , Astellas , AstraZeneca , Bristol Myers , GSK , Merck , Pfizer , and Teva .

It makes arguments similar to the first, noting that the pilot doesn’t account for substantial costs the providers will have to incur by purchasing the drugs at market prices and then applying for rebates.

Listed hospital systems: HCA Healthcare , Community Health Systems , Surgery Partners , Tenet Healthcare , Universal Health Services , Select Medical Holdings (SEM), Acadia Healthcare , LifeStance Health Group

data.title: NEAR Rallies As Quantum-Resistant Upgrade Nears Mainnet And Intents Volume Tops $33B, Arthur Hayes Stays Bullish
data.description:
Key points:
  • NEAR Protocol rallied over 11% on Saturday after the network said its accounts were already protected against future quantum computers.
  • Trading through NEAR Intents, its cross-chain system, passed $33.29 billion in total volume, according to DefiLlama.
  • A draft proposal filed on Wednesday would cut maximum annual token issuance to 1.6% from 2.5% over two years.

NEAR Protocol (NEAR) rallied on Saturday after the protocol said its accounts were already protected against future quantum computers, and trading through its cross-chain system passed $33 billion.

The rally came as NEAR Intents, which lets users move assets between blockchains, reached $33.29 billion in cumulative decentralized exchange (DEX) volume, $4.76 billion of it in the past 30 days, according to DefiLlama.

Total value locked (TVL), the amount of money deposited in the system, stood at roughly $223 million. Of the $7.81 million in fees collected over the month, $2.15 million was used to buy NEAR on the open market and return it to holders.

Intents also sat at the centre of the protocol’s quantum work. The team said it was designing the system’s wallet contracts to accept ML-DSA, a newer type of digital signature built to withstand quantum computers.

NEAR's price rose more than 12% over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, NEAR was among the top trending tickers. Retail sentiment around NEAR remained in the 'neutral' zone, with chatter at 'low' levels over the past day.

Keeping The Coins Safe

Every crypto wallet is locked by a digital signature. It works because nobody can run the maths backwards from your public address to the private key that opens it. A powerful enough quantum computer could one day do exactly that, and the industry calls that moment “Q-day.”

NEAR announced on Friday that its accounts can already use ML-DSA, and that holders do not need to move their coins anywhere to get the protection. A further change, NEP-655, hides account keys entirely and is running on a test network, with a full launch expected within weeks. The protocol said it was designed with quantum in mind in 2018.

Analysts Stay Bullish As NEAR Eyes New Yearly Highs

Analyst Michaël van de Poppe said that NEAR had “such a beautiful chart,” and that a sweep of the lows was bullish from a day-trading view. He said he expected “a little pullback” before the token moved “back upwards towards new yearly highs.” He added that investors should be more bullish this cycle, arguing that if it resembled 2017, returns would be substantial as adoption arrives.

The case was being made in person this week as well. The RollUp founder Andy posted a video showing that Arthur Hayes reportedly remained bullish on NEAR, along with NEAR co-founder Illia Polosukhin joking at the TOKEN2049 Singapore conference about the token reaching triple digits.

data.title: From Washington to Riyadh: visas suspended, missiles fly, and Nobel dreams fade
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Many interesting headlines to pick from this week, including the announcement of the Nobel Prizes. And no.US President Donald Trump is NOT among the winners.that certainly can't be blamed on his self-campaigning falling short, nor on the lack of cheerleaders (like Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif). Guess the Norwegian Nobel Selection Committee found a worthier candidate? More on that later.

First-the US announcement of a freeze on Thursday (8 October) on Green Card filings by eight firms, including India's Tata Consultancy Services and Infosys. The Trump administration also announced probes into nine top universities. Taken together, the moves targeting what is known as the Permanent Labor Certification programme are part of a broader effort to reduce the number of foreign-born people in the US and curtail their ​pathway to residence and citizenship.

Labour secretary Keith Sonderling announced that the suspension would cover IT companies such as Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies, Microsoft, Adobe and Capgemini.

The general verdict in India seems to be that the impact of the twin moves is likely to be minimal, given that Indian IT firms were anticipating the eventuality and consequently reduced their dependence on this route for employment.

What particularly riled, though, were the remarks from US vice president J.D. Vance. "I'm sure that everyone here understands the game that is being played. Bring in indentured servants from outside the country, you lay off American workers, and if you're a corporation, you make a ton of money by undercutting the wages of American workers, replacing them with people who probably should not be in the United States of America to begin with," he said.

The reference to Indian IT workers as "indentured labour" triggered a sharp reaction. The Ministry of External Affairs slammed it as "unwarranted" and "deeply offensive." The US move would not "advance the shared ambitions of both countries," it said, indicating fresh trouble in what is becoming an increasingly beleaguered relationship. "Such descriptions are unwarranted and ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem," the statement said.

It is comments and actions like these that fuel doubts about whether Trump's departure at the end of his term will lead to a change in the US government's outlook towards India. Vance is being seen as a potential successor to Trump. Cracks in the carefully nurtured 25-year-old India-US relationship are widening.

Whether it will lead to a rupture is to be seen. Symptomatic of a transactional US, uncaring about Indian priorities, was Trump's announcement overnight Friday (October) on importing Russian fuel. These are barely weeks after Trump signed into law the Lindsay Graham bill, threatening sanctions on countries like India buying Russian oil.

In other news, Saudi Arabia came under a major attack from Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen this week, with reports that three Saudi nationals were killed in strikes targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The attacks badly damaged a parked aircraft belonging to the national carrier, Saudia, with a pilot among those dead.

"The attack late on Thursday (8 October) was the deadliest in Saudi Arabia since the kingdom and allied forces in neighbouring Yemen launched a major military offensive last weekend against the Iran-backed Houthis," a Guardian newspaper report said. "It was also a significant escalation in the latest front in the Iran war, which has kept oil prices and markets jumpy," it added.

It was being speculated that the aim of the attack was to shut down the kingdom's ​airspace and oil facilities. Carriers such as India's Air India and Akasa Air announced suspensions of flights to Saudi Arabia in the wake of the attacks.

The conflict is adding to the already heightened tensions in the Middle East/West Asia region. And it is now threatening to draw in more countries. Syria this week said it was considering sending troops to Saudi Arabia. That must come as a relief to Saudi Arabia, which had signed a bilateral security pact with Pakistan last year and followed it up with a trilateral pact with Pakistan and Turkey this year. The Mecca Pact has a Nato-like provision which says an attack against one is an attack against all.

Last month, it seemed Pakistan was not keen (or was it not willing?) to do its part in the Mecca pact as the Houthis tightened their control over key islands and the Red Sea coast of Yemen that jeopardised Saudi oil flows from Yanbu port through the Straits of Bab el Mandeb.

Saudi oil shipments through the Hormuz are already blocked due to the US-Iran standoff. News reports said Saudi Arabia, in desperation, sought intelligence assistance from Israel. Recall here that Saudi Arabia has no diplomatic ties with Israel-as yet.

Nato-member Turkey said on Wednesday (7 October) it was sending mainly defensive and technical support-military equipment, intelligence and weapons systems-to help fight the Houthis. ​Pakistan also confirmed to CNN that it was assisting Saudi Arabia. "The forces of Pakistan are already there," Pakistan Army's Lt. Gen. Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry told CNN.

Meanwhile, is the US planning another strike/series of strikes on Iran? A New York Times report said the US military was preparing options to restart major combat operations against Iran. Three aircraft carriers are expected to arrive in West Asia soon. The Pentagon also developed plans to strike Iran's drone capabilities, missile arsenal, energy facilities and other sites. In a social media post on Thursday, Trump said that he would not attack Iran before the midterm polls next month; the two countries were "having productive discussions." Brent crude price on Friday (9 October) fell to $103.53 a barrel from $106 on Wednesday; US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) price was at $90.97.

Meanwhile, in a move that could drive anti-US sentiments high and prove detrimental to long-term interests, US defence secretary -- sorry - secretary of war, Pete Hegseth has said the execution by firing squad of a former US Army major, who shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at the Fort Hood base in 2009, would be livestreamed. Nidal Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, is set to become the first person to be executed by firing squad by the US military since 1945. It is to take place on 3 December.

The aim of livestreaming the execution? In Hegseth's own words: "We'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public. there's serious consequences for these types of things."

Makes perfect sense-somewhere. But could this public execution heighten the sense of anger and injustice against the US among some in certain corners of the world? And work against US interests?

Irony is that public executions are now exceedingly rare worldwide. And the countries known to conduct them in recent years are Iran and Taliban-run Afghanistan! So would the US, which till recently used to stand up for human rights and human dignity across the world, in this case, be willing to be considered on par with Iran and Afghanistan? Are groups like Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch seized of this??

It's that time of the year-when the Nobel Prizes are announced. It's perhaps the most coveted award of the year-well, certainly by Trump anyway. (His case for getting the award was built on stopping eight/nine/perhaps ten wars? Trump himself isn't sure. Each day, he drops a new number. The one he's started-i.e., the war with Iran-is going nowhere.)

The Nobel Peace Prize winner this year was South Africa's Navanethem "Navi" Pillay for her efforts to promote peace and international law, the Nobel Prize Committee said.

Pillay, a South African of Indian Tamil descent, is a former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. She had been instrumental in ensuring war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted. "At a time of existential challenges-including more wars and conflicts than the world has seen in a long time-international law is no longer just a supplement to peace and security. It is an absolute necessity," the Nobel committee said in a statement.

Born in apartheid South Africa, Pillay, 85, was the first woman to start a law practice in Natal province in 1967. Among the many feathers in her cap are serving as a defence lawyer for South African freedom icon Nelson Mandela and being the first woman of colour to serve on South Africa's High Court.

Her many noteworthy international assignments include chairing the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, which was established by the UN Human Rights Council in 2021. In September 2025, the Commission concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Israel dismissed it as "scandalous."

Meanwhile, Pakistan's Shehbaz Sharif kept up his campaign for Trump. "President Donald Trump played a historic role in advancing peace in South Asia. His timely intervention helped bring Pakistan and India back from the brink and secure a ceasefire, that is holding till today.

In recognition of his outstanding contribution, Pakistan had nominated President Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize. We sincerely hope President's efforts to promote peace and prevent conflict in our region receive due recognition this time. @realDonaldTrump @NobelPrize." The post on X.com had garnered 2.6K likes (on Friday evening). It was also majorly trolled by Indians and Pakistanis alike.

data.title: China Is Building a National Blockchain Network: Will Bitcoin Benefit?
data.description:
China’s top leadership has called for a national blockchain network as one of 19 measures in a new economic blueprint. The same document warns officials against creating bubbles and abandoning the real economy for the virtual one.

A blockchain is a shared digital record kept across many computers. Beijing wants the technology, yet the plan says nothing about Bitcoin or any other cryptocurrency.

What China’s Blockchain Plan Actually Says

The Communist Party’s Central Committee and the State Council, China’s cabinet, issued the policy on October 9. State news agency Xinhua carried it on the government’s website the same day.

The blockchain line sits beside a nationwide computing grid, in a section on merging traditional industry with digital technology.

It also backs “East Data, West Computing,” which sends data from eastern cities to western data centers. Separately, it calls for rules on who owns and trades data.

China already runs a state-backed system, the Blockchain-based Service Network (BSN), launched in April 2020.

It does not allow independent cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, according to Stanford’s DigiChina project. The new document does not say whether the national network will build on it.

The plan hands follow-up work to the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission and the National Development and Reform Commission. Their rules will show what the network carries and whether crypto stays shut out.

Why Bitcoin Sits Outside China’s Plan

Crypto trading remains illegal in mainland China. In February, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) and seven other agencies restated that ban.

Beijing’s digital money push runs through its own currency. In August, the PBOC’s five-year plan pledged to steadily develop the digital yuan, China’s state-issued digital currency, according to Xinhua.

The blueprint landed three days after Joseph Chee, chief executive of Nasdaq-listed Solana Company, spoke on CNBC.

“I think the crypto is going to go through another super cycle,” he said.

Chee tied that outcome to Beijing allowing access to trading, BeInCrypto reported earlier this week. He named capital flight as the bigger obstacle and gave no timeline.

data.title: SEBI to issue closing auction session guidelines in a week, says Tuhin Kanta Pandey
data.description:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) hopes to issue guidelines on changes to the closing auction session (CAS) within a week, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Saturday, according to Moneycontrol. Speaking at an event organised by the BSE Brokers’ Forum (BBF) in Mumbai, he said the regulator was examining feedback on a consultation paper addressing concerns over the settlement price of derivatives on expiry days.

Pandey said SEBI would focus on deepening India's cash markets and improving price discovery over the next decade. Greater participation, stronger securities borrowing and lending, and more efficient hedging and arbitrage could help improve liquidity and market efficiency, he said.

The regulator is also reviewing rules governing depositories and their participants to simplify regulations and strengthen fraud prevention. For brokers, SEBI is considering graded compliance requirements based on their size, client exposure and reliance on technology.

SEBI is separately working on changes to clearing arrangements for tender offers, buybacks and offers for sale that remain outside the interoperability framework. These transactions require parallel clearing arrangements, increasing costs and compliance requirements. The regulator is targeting the implementation of these changes by the end of November 2026, Pandey said.

The regulator has also invited comments on simplifying digital onboarding for people residing outside India, including non-resident Indians, without requiring them to be physically present. The consultation has received more than 400 comments, he said.

SEBI will also issue guidelines on the responsible use of artificial intelligence and machine learning. The proposed framework will follow a tiered approach and include clear accountability, data controls, kill switches and human oversight.

In addition, the regulator is strengthening business continuity and disaster recovery systems, cybersecurity safeguards and governance across market infrastructure institutions.

On investor awareness, Pandey said SEBI aimed to expand investor education programmes to universities and colleges across the country. Brokers and other market intermediaries would also need to play an active role in these efforts.

Pandey said India should aim to build a securities market that attracts global investment and sets international standards, combining scale with resilience, speed with safety, and innovation with responsibility.

data.title: Persistent to squeeze out existing Nagarro shareholders en route to become seventh-largest
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Persistent Systems is on track to become the seventh-largest tech services firm in the country after lifting its stake in the German software engineering firm to 94%, a level that can enable a buyout of existing Nagarro shareholders into a merged entity, under German regulations.

The move effectively removes the biggest uncertainty around Persistent's $1.3 billion acquisition, announced in June, and sets the stage for integrating Nagarro into its operations.

Beyond adding nearly $1 billion in annual revenue, the deal significantly expands Persistent's presence in Europe, a market that will account for a much larger share of the combined company's business.

For Persistent, the acquisition is about more than scale; it could propel the company higher in India's IT industry rankings. Investors will now focus on execution, debt repayment, and whether the promised benefits justify the acquisition cost.

"Having secured more than 90% of Nagarro's share capital and voting rights, Persistent plans a squeeze-out of the remaining minority shareholders of Nagarro upon closing. No final decision has been taken yet," the company said in its press release on 9 October.

The Pune-based company progressed in three phases.

Persistent's €81-a-share bid for Nagarro, announced in June, gave it 83% ownership by 17 September. A secondary offer later boosted its stake to 94%, paving the way for a full takeover.

For this, the company paid about $1.1 billion, of which $824 million came from the tendered shares and $253 million from Lantano's stake sale. Persistent Systems isn't paying the acquisition amount out of its own pocket.

In December 2025, the company set up a wholly owned German subsidiary, Galaxy Germany Holding SE, which borrowed up to €1.4 billion ($1.6 billion) from Barclays. This is more than the $1.3 billion that it expected to come from Nagarro's share repurchase. The company would also have to repay the entire loan amount within 18 months, according to the loan terms.

Still, the company's plans to acquire an additional 10% did not come out of the blue. Under German law, if a company holds more than 90% of the target entity's shares, the remaining minority shareholders who have not tendered their shares must sell them to the acquiring entity, which will then have to merge the target into itself. In this case, Persistent will have to merge Nagarro into its German entity and remove the entity from the Frankfurt stock exchange.

At least one brokerage said this would help Nagarro's integration with Persistent.

"A stake above 90% reduces friction in integration. Funding of the acquisition will be partly through debt and partly equity," said Kotak Institutional Equities analysts Kawaljeet Saluja, Sathishkumar S, and Vamshi Krishna, in a note dated 28 September.

This gains significance as Persistent Systems seeks to jump two spots in Indian it's pecking order at a time when tech firms are buying growth to offset AI-led revenue deflation. The management stated that the acquisition is expected to be completed by March next year.

Once complete, the combined Persistent-Nagarro Group will have at least $2.7 billion in revenue.Persistent ended last year with $1.65 billion in revenue, up 17.4%, making it the second-fastest growing tech services firm in the country after Coforge Ltd, which grew 29%.

On the other hand, Nagarro ended the last fiscal year with $999 million in revenue and about 18,500 employees. Almost half of its revenue comes from European clients, a key benefit of the deal, according to Persistent. After the acquisition, Persistent expects one-fifth of its business to come from Europe, up from one-tenth. Persistent's management expects the combined entity to have an annual revenue run rate of $2.9 billion.

For now, Persistent chief executive Sandeep Kalra said shareholders gave a thumbs up to the acquisition.

"The final results of our offer for Nagarro are a clear endorsement of the strategic logic behind bringing Persistent and Nagarro together. We now look forward to completing the remaining steps toward closing. Together, we will build the global AI-led digital engineering player we envision," said Kalra, as part of the company's press release.

Still, at least one analyst is not gung-ho on this acquisition.

"We believe the recent large acquisitions done by the prominent Tier-2 companies like Persistent Systems and Coforge are return dilutive and may pose execution challenges. They also seem to be funded partly or fully through stock dilution," said Bank of Baroda Capital Markets analysts Girish Pai and Lopa Notaria, in a note dated 9 October.

data.title: Godrej DEI Lab Unveils Gateway Programme To Bring Experienced Women Back To Work
data.description:
The initiative aims to help women return to work after career breaks through structured onboarding, coaching and cohort-based learning

Godrej DEI Lab, the diversity, equity and inclusion arm of the Godrej Industries group, has launched Gateway, a returnship programme designed to help experienced women professionals re-enter the workforce after career breaks linked to motherhood, marriage or caregiving. The initiative was announced at the finale of the second edition of India Included on Campus 2026, a case study competition focused on workplace inclusion. It aligns with the group’s target of achieving 40% inclusion of women, LGBTQIA+ individuals and people with disabilities by 2031.

Structured Return To Work

Gateway is designed to create a more structured route for professionals returning after extended career breaks. The programme includes structured onboarding, cohort-based learning and coaching to help participants integrate into mainstream hiring and workplace teams.

The initiative focuses on making career re-entry more accessible to experienced professionals whose skills may remain relevant despite time away from formal employment. It also seeks to address challenges associated with returning to mid-management roles, where employers may need to reassess experience, skills and readiness after a career break.

Sumit Mitra, Group Head of Human Resources and Corporate Services at Godrej Industries, said the programme aims to bring experienced mid-management talent back into the workforce and make return-to-work opportunities more visible.

Career Breaks Among Women

The programme draws on findings from the 2026 study The Missing Half, which highlights that 74% of educated women in India take career breaks. The study was used as a reference point for the case study competition, which asked students to examine barriers faced by women seeking to return to work.

Career interruptions linked to caregiving and family responsibilities can affect professional continuity and access to opportunities. Returnship programmes seek to provide a formal pathway for candidates to demonstrate their capabilities and transition back into employment.

B-School Teams Develop Solutions

The second edition of India Included on Campus 2026 brought together students from institutions including IIM Lucknow, IIT Delhi, XIM Bhubaneswar and SIBM Pune. Participants were asked to develop proposals addressing challenges faced by women returning to professional roles.

XIM Bhubaneswar emerged as the winning team, receiving a cash prize of Rs 1 lakh for its proposal for a structured returnship framework.

Parmesh Shahani, Head of Godrej DEI Lab, said the initiative was intended to translate ideas on inclusion into workplace solutions supported by peer networks and leadership involvement.

Focus On Workplace Inclusion

Gateway adds a return-to-work component to Godrej Industries’ broader inclusion target for 2031. Its implementation will be relevant to how employers structure recruitment, onboarding and support for professionals returning after career breaks.

The programme also highlights the role of employer-led initiatives in addressing gaps between experienced talent and available employment opportunities.

data.title: Avenue Supermarts Q2 Revenue Rises 18% To Rs 19,206 Cr, Profit Up 8%
data.description:
Strong performance from older DMart stores supported quarterly growth, even as wage inflation increased operating costs during the period

Avenue Supermarts, the operator of DMart retail stores, reported a 7.6 per cent year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 804 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. The company’s profit, however, was below the Bloomberg estimate of Rs 879 crore.

Revenue from operations increased 18.4 per cent to Rs 19,206 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 16,219 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The strong revenue growth was supported by continued expansion of the company’s store network and growth in its existing stores.

The company’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 14.1 per cent to Rs 1,403 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 1,230 crore a year earlier. The figure was below the Bloomberg estimate of Rs 1,468 crore.

EBITDA margin, meanwhile, declined to 7.3 per cent from 7.6 per cent in Q2FY26. The margin also fell short of the 7.7 per cent market estimate, indicating pressure on profitability despite the increase in revenue.

Avenue Supermarts added 15 stores during the quarter, taking forward its retail expansion strategy. The company continued to focus on expanding its physical presence while maintaining its pricing proposition across the network.

Older Stores Gain Momentum

Anshul Asawa, Managing Director and CEO of Avenue Supermarts, said stores that were two years old or more recorded 9.5 per cent growth during Q2FY27, compared with 6.8 per cent in the year-ago quarter. The improvement points to stronger performance from the company’s established stores.

Asawa said the company’s pricing proposition remained strong despite the inflationary environment. He added that wage inflation at the entry level had resulted in a marginal increase in operating expenses during the quarter.

The company reported earnings per share of Rs 12.32 for Q2FY27, compared with Rs 1.47 in Q2FY26. The quarterly performance reflected strong top-line growth, although profitability remained below analyst expectations amid pressure on operating margins.

data.title: Vaidehee Chaudhari wins third Fenesta Open title; Maan Kesharwani claims maiden men's crown
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Top seed Vaidehee Chaudhari and sixth seed Maan Kesharwani clinched the women's and men's singles titles, respectively, at the 31st Fenesta Open National Tennis Championship at the DLTA Complex in New Delhi on Saturday.

Chaudhari, who also won the title in 2022 and 2024, defeated 20-year-old Shruti Ahlawat 6-4, 7-5 in a closely contested final that lasted two hours and 15 minutes to secure her third Fenesta Open crown.

"I feel so proud. This is my third title so definitely I am very happy right now," Chaudhari said after the win, as per a press release.

"The first set I was 5-3 up and she kept fighting. Even the second set, I was 5-3 up and she kept fighting till the end. It was a great and a close match," she said.

In the men's singles final, Kesharwani defeated third seed Nitin Sinha 6-0, 6-4 in one hour and 37 minutes to claim his maiden Fenesta Open title.

Kesharwani made a dominant start, winning the first six games to take the opening set without dropping a game. The second set was more competitive, but the sixth seed secured a crucial break at 3-2 before holding his serve to close out the match.

"The first set was easy. But I will congratulate my opponent," Kesharwani said.

"He is a little bit injured but still he is playing and competing. So proud of him. In the second set, it was a little bit shaky. But at 3-2, I broke him, and then I was just holding my serves and I won. This is my first Fenesta title. Since the last 4 years, I was losing in the first round in every Fenesta Open. This time I directly made the finals and won. I am very emotional. I do not know how to express it in words but I am so happy. I would like to specially thank my parents, who have always supported me."

The presentation ceremony was attended by Rohit Rajpal, president of the Delhi Lawn Tennis Association; Saket Jain, Executive Director and Business Head, Fenesta Building Systems; Indian hockey player and 2026 Asian Games gold medallist Jugraj Singh; and Prerna Bhambri, a four-time Fenesta Open champion and treasurer of the Delhi Lawn Tennis Association (DLTA). They presented the trophies to the winners.

"I am very happy to be here," Singh said after the presentation ceremony. "This is the first time I am watching a live match of the Tennis Nationals. I saw a lot of movement in these matches as well. Their shots, receiving the ball and their footwork, I was very happy to watch the matches. I want to say good luck to all the players who have won and to all the others who participates."

Jain reflected on DCM Shriram's nearly three-decade association with Indian tennis through the Fenesta Open and highlighted the company's continued commitment to player development.

"At DCM Shriram, we deeply believe in this journey of growth," he said. "Our association with Indian tennis through the Fenesta Open spans over three decades. Over the years, this championship has been about more than organising a tournament. It has been about creating opportunities, nurturing talent and providing Indian players with a platform to test themselves, gain exposure and take the next step in their sporting careers. That is why we are taking our commitment a step further this year."

"In addition to the championship prize money, we have introduced an additional Rs 11 lakh Player Development Scholarship from our CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) budgets to support the winners and runners-up in their journey ahead. The scholarship will help players invest in essential aspects of their development, including coaching, physiotherapy, fitness and tennis equipment. We hope this initiative helps players invest in their development and pursue their aspirations with greater confidence," he added.

Sixteen-year-old Ribhav Saroha, the 10th seed, upset fourth seed Om Ramesh Patel 6-4, 6-3 to win the boys' U-18 singles title.

"I have played Om many times before and before this match our head-to-head was 3-3. I knew that he is a guy who does not miss any ball and I have to work really really hard. I was really prepared that I have to work the balls and I have to be more consistent than him and I have to be aggressive as well. I played really well and I had a strategy to be consistent and aggressive at the same time. I was able to maintain that strategy," said Saroha.

Reflecting on his experience at the DLTA, Saroha said, "I played Fenesta three years ago for the first time and I played the qualifying of the U14s and for me it is like the Indian Grand Slam. The facilities are really superb and everything is on the mark. It's really excellent to play on these courts and I feel so happy to win this U18 Fenesta Nationals being a 16-year-old."

In the girls' U-18 singles final, second seed Parthsarthi Mundhe defeated seventh seed Aahan Aahan 6-3, 6-4 to lift the title.

"It was not a very easy match but it was a good one," Mundhe said after the win. "She was rallying and there were long rallies in the match. This tournament has been a very good experience actually. This is my first tournament after five months. It was a very great experience that I reached the finals and could win it."

The action now shifts to the Fenesta Open U-16 and U-14 events, which kick off next week at DLTA.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Says French Debt Crisis Could Send Bitcoin To $250,000 As AI Debt Risks Mount
data.description:
Key points:
  • Arthur Hayes said he thinks a French financial crisis could force the Fed and Treasury to manufacture money, pushing Bitcoin higher.
  • France's 10-year government bond yield momentarily exceeded 5% on October 1 and 2, its highest level since 2002.
  • If the crisis scenario develops, Hayes anticipates Bitcoin to trade between $125,000 and $250,000 by year-end.

Arthur Hayes believes that problems in France's bond market could propel Bitcoin (BTC) to a new high. The BitMEX co-founder stated that a French debt crisis would push the Fed and U.S. Treasury to issue money.

Hayes, speaking after his TOKEN2049 Singapore speech with CryptoBanter on Thursday, labeled France the weak link, cited its high government expenditure in relation to the size of its economy, claiming that few investors want its debt. Bond markets are already under stress. France's 10-year yield momentarily surpassed 5% on October 1 and 2, the highest level since 2002.

Its premium over German bonds has increased to approximately 152 basis points, the highest since 2011. The government intends to borrow a record €340 billion next year. Yields have dipped since then, although they remain about 4.8%.

In such a scenario, Bitcoin could benefit with the low end being close to Bitcoin's previous record of approximately $126,000, seen in October last year. He believes Bitcoin will trade between $125,000 and $250,000 before the end of the year if that case holds out.

Bitcoin’s price was trading at around $82,751, down 0.5% in the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, as chatter stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

Could Help US Retire Its Entire Treasury Debt?

Hayes said the U.S. would respond with a gold revaluation. “I would monetize gold and essentially depreciate the dollar against gold,” he said. He said he would set the price for gold at $50,000 to $60,000 per ounce.

The gain would allow Washington to retire the whole stock of Treasury securities. Hayes predicted that the move would be significantly inflationary. He described it as the only method he sees to deal with excessive debt and high interest payments.

Hayes Warns AI Data Center Debt Could Trigger A 2008-Style Crisis

Hayes also finds risk in investing in AI. The U.S. economy is so heavily dependent on building data centers, they’re like real estate projects, he said. That means if tenants can’t pay, lenders will cease financing new developments.

The waste could become obvious in 2027 and 2028, he said. Bad debt could then extend to insurers and fiduciaries, as it happened in 2008. Hayes anticipates governments will print money to make insurers whole, rather than allow AI to cause a recession.

Soaring sovereign yields are squeezing out AI funding, he said. Hyperscalers care less about the increased costs of debt because they see the benefit of constructing advanced AI as endless, Hayes said. Countries like France are the ones that are squeezed.

data.title: AI euphoria faces concern as bubble warnings intensify
data.description:
The artificial-intelligence boom has sent the market roaring but now several analysts, investors, and policymakers are warning that the bubble may be approaching its breaking point.

Concerns that initially centered on skyrocketing corporate debt to finance the massive data centers and rising interest rates have since escalated, with industry leaders now saying that advances in AI could potentially cause catastrophic harm to humanity within the next decade.

In an unusual display of solidarity, the heads of many AI labs came together last month to say that the progress of improving AI model capabilities should be scaled back.

In the face of potential risks, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called to 'slow the pace' of AI model improvements and urged for greater coordination among AI companies, with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX founder Elon Musk agreeing with Amodei. This came after an Anthropic insider Evan Hubinger said in a post on X that he "earnestly" believes AI could kill all humans, putting his personal estimate of the probability at more than 10% within the next decade.

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates also stated that the technology is “powerful enough” to help cause at least 1B human deaths. This week, Anthropic , OpenAI , and other companies’ top executives are reportedly gaming out scenarios for a public and political revolt following a catastrophic AI event.

Here are some prominent investors, strategists, and analysts who warned that the AI bubble could burst

Ray Dalio

The billionaire has sounded the alarm on the AI bubble, warning that it is nearing the point where it may burst due to rising interest rates and increased borrowing to fund the AI infrastructure buildout.

"What creates the bursting of a bubble is the fact that you need cash," he said. "And you start to convert the wealth that you have to do that. Something like a wealth tax would have that effect, or having to pay back loans. So there's that dynamic that we have to keep an eye on."

Joachim Klement:

The London investment-bank strategist sees a scenario in which the AI-driven rally unravels as soon as 2027, dragging the broader market sharply lower.

“My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement said in an interview and urged clients to prepare for such a scenario rather than wait for the selloff to begin.

Michael Burry

The famous “Big Short” investor caution that the AI boom could resemble past speculative market episodes. He took short positions against high-flying tech and industrial stocks, including Nvidia , Oracle , Palantir , Nebius , Micron , CoreWeave , and has repeatedly challenged the AI investment narrative. He has argued that enormous capital spending might not necessarily translate into durable returns.

Michael Novogratz

The Galaxy Digital CEO said it is in the "biggest bubble of our lifetime" but advised investors to ride the wave rather than exit immediately.

Sam Altman:  

Last year, the OpenAI CEO has reportedly said that he believes AI could be in a bubble and compared the market conditions to those of the dotcom boom in the 1990s.

data.title: Cirrus Logic is said to have made a rival bid for Synaptics after Onsemi offer
data.description:
Cirrus Logic has offered to acquire Synaptics in September, as the semiconductor company looked to fend off a competing bid from ON Semiconductor Corporation , Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The report came after onsemi agreed to acquire Synaptics for $123 per share in an all-cash deal worth roughly $5.7B last week, revising its previous all-stock bid worth about $7B disclosed in June.

Onsemi changed the deal terms following an “unsolicited competing proposal” from a third party, according to a statement, which didn’t name the bidder.

Austin-based Cirrus Logic is the "Party A" mentioned in an updated proxy filing from Synaptics on Thursday, the people said, asking for anonymity as details are private.

The filing indicated that board members of Synaptics seriously evaluated Cirrus Logic’s cash and stock bid and even held discussions with the company before eventually settling on Onsemi's revised offer.

It’s unclear if Cirrus Logic continues to have buyout interest in Synaptics, the people added.

Representatives for both Cirrus Logic and Onsemi declined to comment on the report, according to Bloomberg. Synaptics didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: America's hottest pizza chains might be gas station operators
data.description:
Convenience stores and gas stations across the country are increasingly serving up made-to-order pizza that rivals what customers get from traditional pizzerias in a phenomenon that is starting to reshape the competitive map for the industry. A recent pizza-industry research report noted that gas station pizza, long dismissed as low-quality food hardening all day under heat lamps, is improving enough that it's now considered a serious and fast-rising competitor eating into pizzeria profits, especially in small towns without as many dine-in and delivery options.

Casey's General Stores , which operates roughly 2,600 locations across the Midwest and beyond, has leaned heavily into low-cost fresh food offerings, including pizza and bakery items. Notably, Casey's built its pizza business by turning convenience stores into neighborhood pizzerias, particularly in small towns underserved by major restaurant chains. By installing on-site ovens and kitchens rather than simply selling reheated pizza, the convenience store chain has established a reputation for serving quality pizza and boosted customer loyalty. The pizza business expanded alongside Casey’s store network through a rural strategy that includes new construction, acquisitions, and investments in kitchens. The company also developed its own distribution network, helping maintain consistent supplies and control logistics costs across locations.

Also in the mix, Hunt Brothers Pizza is a family-owned, Nashville-based pizza business founded in 1991 by four brothers. Rather than operating stand-alone restaurants, the company supplies a branded pizza program to convenience stores and gas stations, particularly in rural communities with limited restaurant options. The chain is now found in more than 11K locations across 33 states. While quality can vary across locations, Hunt Brothers scores very high on consumer review sites in comparison to national pizza chains.

Over the last year, Domino's has snapped up market share from rivals such as Pizza Hut and Papa John's even as it faces the new threat in rural areas from the gas station operators with updated pizza ovens.

data.title: The Real Challenge For Muse AI Is Making The Math Make Sense — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Adam Levine

Meta Platforms' Muse personal AI agent is an early hit, holding the iOS App Store top spot since soon after its Sept. 8 release. According to research from Human Security, it was already the No. 1 agent last month, responsible for 40% of agent-based traffic on the internet. Largely because of its release, agent traffic tripled in a month.

Meta stock is up 18% since Muse's release.

But Meta is probably losing money on Muse now, and it will be very hard for it to defray the costs down the line.

As it demonstrated with its Threads microblogging platform, Meta's strategy is to scale a new product and then monetize it with ads. But Muse may be different, because it's promising to bring a level of privacy and security to it that Meta isn't known for. Soon, interactions with Muse will be opaque to everyone aside from the user, including Meta. The kind of highly effective ad targeting that Meta's data collection enables in Facebook and Instagram may not work as well in Muse. If user behavior in Muse is anonymized, it won't provide Meta with data to further refine its targeting.

In any case, Meta isn't yet talking about ads in Muse. For now, it is looking to e-commerce and premium subscriptions to subsidize the costs.

And those costs may be very high. At least to begin with, Meta is being very generous with the Muse free tier, allocating up to 100 million tokens a week for each user. Tokens are the basic unit of artificial-intelligence text; for example, this sentence is made up of about 30 tokens when measured by common methods. Though we don't know exactly what the computing costs of 100 million tokens are to Meta, we have a decent idea of what it would charge if someone were using the underlying model, Muse Spark, to do other things like writing software code using the company's application programming interface, or API.

On the API, there are different prices for tokens depending on how they are being used, with the cheapest being "cache" tokens. Even if 97% of a Muse user's tokens are for cache, free-tier users are getting the equivalent of an $1,100 annual API credit. In the past 12 months, Meta has generated only $63.54 per each of its 3.6 billion daily app users, almost entirely through ads. The tough job ahead of Meta is bridging that gap for Muse.

It's unclear what Meta's profit margin is on the Muse Spark API, but we can deduce that it isn't as high as the top models from OpenAI and Anthropic. In the "cost per task" metric of research firm Artificial Analysis, Muse Spark is closer to inexpensive Chinese models than the ones from the U.S. frontier AI labs. The Muse Spark API is a great deal for users, and Meta may well be underpricing it to gain market share.

Revenue per user from the Muse agent is likely going to have to be much higher than what Meta earns from its apps to recoup the costs. If Meta were able to capture all of Visa's revenue with its Muse e-commerce fees — $45 billion in the past 12 months — that could be enough, but scaling to the size of Visa won't be easy.

This year, Meta intends to spend up to $145 billion on capital expenditures for new AI data centers.

The Muse math gets even tougher for Meta in the paid tiers. The $240-a-year plan offers the equivalent of $5,500 in annual API credit, and the $1,200-a-year tier comes with a staggering $33,000 of annual credit. On the free tier, where most of the casual users of Muse will be, Meta can count on many of them not coming close to their free token allocation, bringing average token use down. But people on the paid plans will likely be power users who will be using Muse to run their lives like a full-time human personal assistant would. They may come close to using up their entire token budget every week.

Meta didn't respond to a request for comment on the wide gulf between its average revenue per user and Muse token allocations.

The company is hoping that everyone becomes a power user, and that they make Muse a daily habit like its social-media apps. But the more successful Muse is, and the more people use it, the more difficult profitability will become.

This dovetails with a recent report from research firm SemiAnalysis, which showed that the API costs of the token allocations for OpenAI and Anthropic subscription plans are well in excess of their subscription prices. In effect, at all three companies, API customers are subsidizing free and subscription users.

The situation is indicative of where we are right now in AI. The costs are evident in the hundreds of billions of dollars being spent for new AI data centers. Cloud providers like Amazon.com, Microsoft, and Alphabet are earning revenue from renting out these servers, but companies with no cloud service like Meta are fishing around for income, and it isn't clear exactly where the profits come from when the expenses are so high.

Meanwhile, Meta shareholders have to endure reduced operating profit margins, down to 37% in the latest quarter (after excluding some one-time charges) from 43% last year. Making Muse a mass-market service is going to be no mean feat, but making it a profitable one may prove the bigger hill to climb.

data.title: ED arrests Sadhna Group MD over money-laundering allegations: Who is Rakesh Gupta? What's the Rs.168 crore case?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Dr Rakesh Gupta, chairman and managing director of Sadhna Group, has been arrested. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has detailed him in a money-laundering case involving alleged criminal proceeds. The agency estimates these proceeds at about Rs.168 crore.

A court sent Gupta to five days of ED custody early on 10 October. Gupta's arrest took place at Ishwar Farms. The group runs Sadhna TV and other media networks.

Gupta, 63, is the founder, chairman and managing director of Delhi-based Sadhna Group. The group operates channels covering spiritual programmes, culture and regional news.

These include Sadhna TV, Ishwar TV, Sadhna Plus News and Har Khabar. Sadhna TV has over 3.9 million subscribers on YouTube.

Gupta has a YouTube channel called "The Dr Rakesh Gupta Show Plus Minus". He presents himself as a senior journalist and mentor. The YouTube channel has 18,700 subscribers.

His programmes cover motivational stories, startups, UPSC success and ancient Indian history. They also highlight local innovators and businesspeople who address social problems. On social media, he invites young entrepreneurs to share business ideas.

His business interests include a Bio-CNG plant in Mathura, solar installations and outdoor advertising. His companies also hold marketing rights across various metro stations.

The ED investigation follows a Delhi Police Economic Offences Wing FIR registered on 29 September. The police case includes allegations of cheating and criminal breach of trust. Gupta is named as the second accused.

The ED alleges that Gupta arranged Sadhna Media Pvt Ltd's insolvency through connected creditors. Such creditors held 99.41% of the committee of creditors. According to ED, income-tax dues of Rs.110.10 crore were settled for Rs.20 lakh.

The agency alleges that the company paid Rs.4.48 crore to connected creditors. This included about Rs.2.99 crore paid to Gupta's company, Sharpline Broadcast Ltd.

It also alleges cash receipts of Rs.2.50 crore to Rs.2.82 crore. These allegedly came through USDT and hawala channels during SMPL/Aryan TV's resale.

The ED further cited a SEBI order concerning alleged Sadhna Broadcast Ltd share manipulation. It said SEBI identified Gupta as the mastermind and held him, along with others, liable. The amount involved was about Rs.58 crore.

Investigators want to trace cash, examine seized devices and check company records. They also seek details about Rs.8.98 crore payable without any bank trail.

The court granted five days' custody, considering Gupta's age and the specific tasks of the investigation. He must appear again on 15 October by 4 PM.
